title: Define customer-facing docs deliverables + owners for SIEM-ready audit export beta
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Goal
Define the minimum customer-facing documentation set required for SIEM-ready audit export (beta), including owners, review requirements, and acceptance criteria so we can onboard design partners consistently and pass enterprise security reviews.

Scope (docs deliverables)
This ticket is about WHAT we need to publish (and who owns each piece), not writing the docs in this ticket.

Customer-facing doc set for beta
1) Landing / Overview ("SIEM-ready audit export (beta)")
- Purpose and value prop (SIEM correlation-ready audit events)
- Supported sinks (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3)
- Deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
- Delivery semantics summary (at-least-once, duplicates possible)
- High-level filtering capabilities and examples
- Known limitations for beta + what’s explicitly not supported
Owner: Elliot Price (Docs)
Reviewers: Naomi Feldman (PM), Marcus Lin (Security Eng)

2) Setup Guide: Splunk HEC
- Prereqs (HEC enabled, token/index, TLS requirements)
- Destination configuration fields and examples
- Test delivery steps + what to expect in Splunk
- Common errors and troubleshooting (401/403 token, HEC 5xx, HEC ACK optional)
- Suggested parsing/search queries and dashboard starter notes
Owner: Kira Thompson (Tech writer)
SME: Kevin Osei (Security Eng), Colin O’Donnell (Solutions)

3) Setup Guide: Datadog Logs intake
- Picking the right intake endpoint (region)
- API key scoping and recommended permissions
- Destination configuration examples
- Tag mapping suggestions (tenant/workspace/env)
- Troubleshooting rate limits (429) and partial failures
Owner: Kira Thompson (Tech writer)
SME: Fatima Noor (Solutions), Allison Grant (Observability)

4) Setup Guide: S3 (including SSE-KMS)
- Bucket prerequisites, path/partitioning overview (tenant/date/hour)
- Encryption options: SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS (recommended)
- IAM least-privilege guidance (read/write/list, KMS permissions)
- Object format/compression notes (gzip), expected event structure
- Duplicate object/event guidance and best practices
Owner: Kira Thompson (Tech writer)
SME: Diego Santos (Platform), Hanae Suzuki (Secrets/KMS)

5) Dedupe + Idempotency Guidance (required for all sinks)
- Clear statement of at-least-once semantics
- Dedupe key: which fields to use (event_id + schema_version + destination_id where relevant)
- Ordering expectations (no strict ordering guarantees across partitions)
- How to handle replays (possible intentional duplicates)
- SIEM-specific notes: Splunk indexing behavior, Datadog ingestion, S3 batch processing
Owner: Elliot Price (Docs)
SME: Ethan Park (Control plane), Sean Gallagher (SRE)
Security review: Marcus Lin

6) Filtering Reference + Examples
- Supported filter dimensions for beta (event_type, actor, workspace/tenant, environment, time window; optional IP/region if enabled)
- Semantics (include/exclude precedence, default behavior)
- Validation errors (what users see in Console)
- Recommended baseline filters to reduce noise without losing security-relevant events
Owner: Elliot Price (Docs)
SME: Benji Okafor (Control plane), Kevin Osei (Security Eng)

7) Limitations / Beta Caveats (single source of truth)
- Explicit non-goals for beta (no broad vendor coverage, limited backfill, no custom field mapping)
- Known failure modes and what “degraded” looks like
- Operational caveats (latency during peak, backpressure, connector-side throttling)
- Support boundaries (what Support/SE can do in beta; replay is operator-assisted)
Owner: Naomi Feldman (PM)
Reviewers: Sean Gallagher (SRE), Rafael Mendes (SRE)

8) Security Posture FAQ (customer-facing)
- Data handled (audit events), PII/redaction rules, retention expectations
- Credential handling (where stored, encryption, rotation)
- Tenant isolation model
- Delivery guarantees statement (no exactly-once)
- Private deployment specifics (egress, customer-managed KMS)
Owner: Marcus Lin (Security Eng)
Writer: Elliot Price (Docs)
Compliance review: Olga Petrov (GRC)

9) Release Notes (beta)
- Feature-flagged release and enablement requirements
- Supported sinks and schema version
- Migration notes for schema v1 changes
- “What’s new / known issues” section
Owner: Naomi Feldman (PM)
Writer: Elliot Price (Docs)

Where docs live / publishing plan
- External: Redwood Docs site (redwood-docs repo) under Security → Audit Logging → Audit Export (Beta)
- Internal (support/ops): Confluence links for runbooks, SLOs, and replay tooling (not all content is customer-visible)
- If we must ship during beta with partial coverage, we still require #1 (overview), #2/#3/#4 (at least one sink guide for each supported sink), and #5 (dedupe guidance).

Acceptance criteria
- Owners assigned and confirmed for each deliverable above.
- Review checklist defined:
  - Security sign-off required for: Overview, Dedupe Guidance, Security FAQ, any statements about encryption/retention/PII.
  - SRE sign-off required for: Limitations/Beta Caveats and any operational guidance.
- Drafts created (even if not published) with clear links from the overview page.
- Language consistency requirements:
  - Use “at-least-once delivery; duplicates possible” wording (do not imply exactly-once).
  - Avoid promises on latency beyond published SLO language.
  - Clarify replay behavior and safeguards.

Open questions
- Do we document optional IP/region filter support in beta, or keep it internal until we have consistent behavior across Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
- For Private: do we provide S3-compatible storage guidance (non-AWS) in beta docs or handle case-by-case via Solutions?

Links / references
- PRD: Confluence (SIEM-ready audit export beta PRD)
- Schema: Audit Event v1 (Confluence)
- Design spec: Filtering + delivery guarantees (Confluence)
- Engineering tracker: ENG-13920

Notes
This doc set is intended to support design partner onboarding + enterprise security questionnaires. Anything that requires operator access (replay tooling, DLQ inspection) should be described as “contact support / solutions” rather than giving direct, self-serve steps unless we’ve shipped the customer-facing workflow in Console.
comments: 2025-02-05 (Naomi Feldman): Added requirement for a single “Limitations/Beta Caveats” source of truth. We’ve had inconsistent messaging in prior betas; want this centralized and linked from every sink guide.

2025-02-07 (Elliot Price): Proposed splitting “Dedupe + Idempotency” into its own page rather than burying per-sink. Splunk/S3 customers need the same conceptual guidance and we should reference it from every setup guide.

2025-02-10 (Marcus Lin): Security review requirement: any mention of encryption, credential storage, or PII/redaction must be approved by Security Eng + GRC. Also ensure docs emphasize that destinations are customer-managed and misconfiguration can lead to data exposure.

2025-02-12 (Sean Gallagher): Please avoid hard numbers for delivery latency in customer docs; reference “target SLOs” only where we have confidence and keep language as expectations/operational notes. Add a short section on what “degraded” means and what customers will see in Console.

2025-02-18 (Naomi Feldman): Owners confirmed with Docs/SE/Security. Proceeding with doc drafts in redwood-docs; will gate publishing behind beta feature flag and only share direct links with onboarded tenants.
